newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel favours easing foreign investor norms.
newsitem.headline: India panel favours easing foreign investor norms.

text.p: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) registered on Indian stock exchanges should be allowed to invest in individual stocks without central bank approval, a Reserve Bank of India panel recommended on Tuesday.
The panel -- which recommended a fully convertible Indian rupee in the next three years -- said authorised foreign exchange dealers would report FII investments.
The panel said it favoured removing the RBI approval requirement on FII investments in primary issues, private placements and divestments of state-run firms.
The panel said it favoured removing the maturity restrictions on investments in debt instruments (including treasury bills).
"FII investments in rupee debt securities to be kept outside the external commercial borrowings (ECB) ceiling but could be part of a separate ceiling," the report stated.
FIIs are currently permitted to invest in dated government securities in the primary and secondary markets. The ECB ceiling includes FII investment in rupee debt instruments.
